stories.headline: European Union Faces Border Crisis as Thousands Enter Spanish Enclave of Ceuta
stories.body:
A massive influx of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta has triggered a political crisis across Europe and led to strict border controls. Ceuta and Melilla are autonomous Spanish cities located on the northern coast of Africa. Together, they form the only land borders that the European Union shares on the African mainland. Since July 29, nearly 60,000 migrants breached the border into Ceuta. At least 67 people died while attempting to reach the enclave from Morocco during the mass surge.

By August 1, the Spanish Interior Ministry reported that nearly all of the 60,000 migrants who crossed the border had departed Ceuta. More than 48,000 of them returned to Morocco within 48 hours of crossing. Despite these departures, Juan Jesús Vivas, the president of Ceuta, stated that several thousand people still need to be returned. Vivas added that the situation inside the enclave has not fully returned to normal.

To stop people from swimming into the enclave, Spanish Civil Guard officers began laying a 500-metre floating pneumatic barrier along the Tarajal breakwater in Ceuta. However, Spanish authorities faced legal limits on immediate returns. A Spanish Supreme Court ruling published on July 8 barred authorities from immediately returning migrants who arrive by sea.

The events in Ceuta quickly spread political tension across Europe. Leaders from 22 of the 27 EU member states signed an open letter demanding an urgent video meeting of interior ministers to coordinate a joint response. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni posted on X that defending the Union's external borders is a shared European responsibility. Italy also temporarily suspended its Schengen-area border-free agreement with Spain for one month following the migrant surge into Ceuta.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez strongly criticized the border decision made by other EU members. Sánchez described the Schengen suspension as a selfish, polarising, and unlawful reaction.

stories.headline: Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv as Ukraine Sinks Russian Ship in Black Sea
stories.body:
An overnight Russian missile and drone barrage against Kyiv killed nine people and injured over 30 others on August 1. In Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, seven people were killed and 14 others were injured after strikes caused widespread fires. The attack also caused damage to Lithuania's embassy in Kyiv when Russian missiles struck near the compound. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russia launched 35 missiles and 185 attack drones during the raid. He noted that Ukrainian forces intercepted only one of 27 ballistic missiles. Zelensky later appealed on social media, writing that every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves lives.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces launched strikes against Russian targets far from the frontline. A sanctioned Russian container ship was sunk in the Black Sea following an attack by Ukrainian drones. Russian state nuclear operator Rosatom confirmed that its 100,000-tonne container ship, the Yanina, was sunk 130 miles from Novorossiysk. Additionally, Ukrainian drone strikes hit three oil refineries in Russia's Bashkortostan region, roughly 1,000 miles from the front lines. In the United States, President Donald Trump stated during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David that the US had not yet agreed to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles under license.

stories.headline: Famed Mountaineer Nirmal Purja Among 10 Killed in Pakistan Avalanche
stories.body:
Renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja and nine other expedition members died in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan. Broad Peak in Northern Pakistan is 26,414 feet high, making it the 12th-highest mountain in the world. Purja had served in the British military for 16 years, including 10 years in the Special Boat Service, and was awarded an MBE in 2018. In 2019, Purja became the first person to climb all 14 world mountains above 8,000 meters in six months and six days.

Pakistani rescue officials recovered the bodies of three climbers following the disaster. The recovered victims were identified as American mountaineer Mallory Geis, 39, of San Antonio, Texas; Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy of Oman; and Pur Bahadur Gurung of Nepal. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah expressed shock at the tragedy in the Karakoram range, which claimed the lives of six Nepalese and four foreign climbers.

stories.headline: Football Governing Bodies Express No Confidence in FIFA President Infantino
stories.body:
European and international football governing bodies have declared a loss of confidence in FIFA President Gianni Infantino following a controversial World Cup investment proposal. Infantino proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise, a plan to value a new commercial subsidiary at $20 billion and raise up to $4.2 billion from private investors. Infantino withdrew the proposal to allow private equity investment following widespread backlash.

Despite the withdrawal of the plan, major football bodies condemned FIFA's leadership. UEFA declared that FIFA leadership under Infantino had lost the confidence of European football and other governing bodies. The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) declared a fundamental breach of trust and stated it no longer has confidence in Infantino. CONCACAF condemned the proposal as a unilateral act of poor governance and called for a full review of Infantino's leadership. Carlos Cordeiro, special adviser to Infantino and senior adviser to the White House Task Force on the 2026 World Cup, resigned amid the backlash. However, Qatar Football Association President Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa bin Ahmed Al Thani applauded Infantino's decision to scrap the plan to prioritize unity among member associations.

stories.headline: US Embassies Urge Citizens to Leave Middle East Amid Escalating Tensions
stories.body:
US embassies across 10 Middle Eastern countries issued security alerts advising American citizens to consider leaving the region due to potential unforeseen escalation. Tensions rose as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that any US aggression or regional assistance to US attacks would meet a proportionate, decisive Iranian response. Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's military central command, warned that any country serving as a defensive shield for the US would be engulfed by war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps asserted full control over the Strait of Hormuz and declared the waterway closed to traffic without its permission.

Military actions have already flared in nearby waters and territory. Kuwait's military stated that its forces destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran targeting government and civilian facilities on Bubiyan Island. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a tanker off Oman was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged its engine room. Meanwhile, EUCOM chief Gen. Alexus Grynkewich warned the Pentagon that the US lacks sufficient naval assets to maintain continuous missile defense operations for Israel against Iranian attacks. US President Donald Trump is considering strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure to force Iran into accepting US ceasefire terms.

stories.headline: Sightseeing Plane Crashes Near Nazca Lines in Peru, Killing All 13 Aboard
stories.body:
A tourist sightseeing plane crashed near the Nazca Lines in southern Peru on August 1, killing all 13 people on board. The aircraft carried 11 passengers and two pilots when it went down in Pueblo Viejo after departing from Pisco. The Cessna Grand Caravan aircraft crashed at 1:20 pm local time after losing contact with the control tower minutes after departure. The plane belonged to local Peruvian sightseeing airline Aerodiana.

Local authorities identified the crash victims as seven Italians, two Germans, two Spanish citizens, and two Peruvian crew members. Flight safety in the region has been a recurring concern, as previous fatal crashes over the Nazca Lines occurred in 2022, 2010, and 2008 due to safety concerns surrounding small tourist flights.

stories.headline: Political Row Grows in India Over Youth Protests and Parliament Skit
stories.body:
Political dispute has intensified in India following recent student protests, allegations of police violence, and a controversial political skit performed inside Parliament. The tensions involve opposition political leaders, independent lawmakers, and student party organizers.

One part of the dispute stems from student demonstrations and police action during a march on July 20. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke demanded a public apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi over alleged police violence against student protesters during that July 20 march. Further protests took place at Jantar Mantar, where some demonstrators targeted the Prime Minister. Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a video message addressing the demonstrations. In his statement, Modi said he forgave students who used abusive language against him during protests at Jantar Mantar, calling them misguided children.

At the same time, severe political pushback emerged over an opposition protest in Parliament. During the protest near Makar Dwar in Parliament, Independent MP Pappu Yadav wore saffron robes and performed a skit portraying a priest stealing money from donation boxes. The skit mocked Ram temple donation theft.

The performance prompted legal action from authorities and complaints from ruling party leaders. Police in Varanasi registered an FIR against Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, as well as MPs Pappu Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad, over the skit mocking Ram temple donation theft in Parliament. Additionally, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj filed a police complaint in Delhi against Opposition MPs. Swaraj accused the lawmakers of making a mockery of Sanatan culture during their Parliament protest.

stories.headline: Torrential Rain Triggers Landslides and Severe Flooding in Kerala
stories.body:
Incessant heavy rain has caused deadly landslides and severe flooding across Kerala, killing at least six people. Four of the recorded deaths occurred in Idukki and Kottayam districts. Two people, including a swimming instructor, were reported missing in rain-related incidents in Kannur district.

The extreme weather caused severe disruption across multiple areas. In Kozhikode district, flooding and landslips forced the evacuation of 214 people into eight relief camps. Authorities in Kozhikode also imposed traffic restrictions on heavy and non-essential vehicles along the Thamarassery ghat road due to landslide risks. In Pala, located in Kottayam district, floodwaters submerged a poultry farm and killed approximately 2,500 chickens. Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan confirmed that 17 houses were completely destroyed and 127 suffered partial damage across the state.

Heavy rainfall is expected to continue across the region. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert forecasting extremely heavy rainfall for eight districts in Kerala, including Pathanamthitta, Idukki, and Kozhikode.
